# Sylvie + Elias Ideas

A private, mobile-first activity picker built from the family notes, OT sensory diet, therapy observations, and app/game research.

## Use What We've Got

The **Our stuff** tab turns things already nearby into practical activity ideas:

1. Mark starter inventory items as available.
2. Add any custom household or play items.
3. Select 1-5 items under **Today we have...**
4. Choose the current need and tap **Find ideas**.

The builder ranks exact and close matches and shows:

- materials used
- child and place fit
- setup and reset time
- clear steps and a parent script
- supervision notes
- a **No shopping needed** badge when all materials are owned

## Guided Play And What Worked

Every regular and use-what-we-have idea now has a **Start this idea** action. Guided play mode provides:

- one parent script and clear checkable steps
- a gentle activity timer with a one-minute finishing cue
- supervision reminders
- a quick **Loved it**, **Worked well**, or **Not today** finish

The **Lately** tab keeps a small private history in that browser so reliable family wins can be repeated. It is not a clinical record and does not leave the device.
That private history can also be downloaded as a JSON backup from the **Lately** tab.

The idea shelf also includes quick-fit filters for five-minute ideas, no-setup ideas, before dinner, bedtime, rainy days, and out-and-about moments.

Starter inventory is maintained in `things-data.js`. It includes art supplies, cardboard/MakeDo, pretend-play resources, outdoor equipment, cosy items, technology, furniture, spaces, and protected special-play items.

## Example Photos And Image Licences

Each original, researched and use-what-we-have activity can show a **relevant photo from Wikimedia Commons** in the spotlight, idea cards, three-step mini-plans and guided play. Photos are loaded lazily to keep the phone interface responsive. Hopscotch missions and selected garden activities use specifically chosen file examples; other activities use hand-curated subject searches, with category fallbacks where needed. Different activities can share a Commons photo. Search results are illustrative examples, not depictions of Sylvie or Elias.

For every displayed photo, the app checks the Wikimedia Commons file's `imageinfo` metadata, accepts Creative Commons/public-domain licences, displays the credited creator and licence, and links to the original file page (and licence link when provided). Results without an identifiable open licence are rejected. Cropping for small preview cards is presentation-only; the full image and licence are available at its source.

**Network and privacy:** Photos require internet access. When an image is about to come into view, the browser contacts `commons.wikimedia.org` for metadata and `upload.wikimedia.org` to load the selected image. This means Wikimedia will see a network request/IP address, but there are no tracking accounts or third-party analytics; requests omit browser cookies and referrer where possible. If a photo cannot load or the app is offline, the app shows a link to example photos rather than falsely presenting an unlicensed image. The rest of the activity instructions and timer work offline.

Image provider: [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/). Example: [Hopscotch game.jpg](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Hopscotch_game.jpg) by Gwasheya, CC0.

## Privacy And Local Storage

There is no backend, account, analytics, tracking, or external AI service.

Custom inventory names, notes, safety reminders, ownership choices, today's selections, and saved favourites are stored only in that browser's `localStorage`. Do not enter private therapy notes, diagnoses, medical details, dates of birth, or other sensitive information.

## Open It On This Computer

Double-click `start-on-phone.ps1`, or run:

```powershell
.\start-on-phone.ps1
```

Then open the local address shown in the terminal.

## Open It On A Phone

1. Connect the phone and this computer to the same Wi-Fi.
2. Run `start-on-phone.ps1`.
3. Open the phone address shown in the terminal.
4. Use the browser's **Add to Home Screen** option if it offers one.

Keep the terminal open while using the app from another device. Favourites are stored separately on each device.

The local Wi-Fi address is plain HTTP, so some phone browsers will not allow offline installation. Hosting the same folder on an HTTPS service enables the full installable/offline behaviour.

## What Is Included

- 192 practical activity ideas
- 30 additional researched indoor and outdoor ideas with source links
- 67 distinct activities and rhythms from the Home-Based Enrichment Program
- Strong outdoor and sensory-diet coverage
- One-tap indoor and outdoor filters
- Dedicated Faith + values ideas
- Filters for Sylvie, Elias, and together play
- Quick ideas for energy, calming, transitions, and after screens
- Three-step mini-plans
- Search, details, safety notes, and locally saved favourites
- 33 structured use-what-we-have ideas
- Custom local-only inventory and a Today we have selector
- Matching by material, child, indoor/outdoor, energy, category, need, and setup time
- Guided play mode with checkable steps and a gentle timer
- Private activity outcomes and recent wins
- Six quick-fit real-life filters

## Project Structure

- `index.html` - semantic page structure
- `styles.css` - mobile-first styling
- `app.js` - original idea picker, filters, favourites, and mini-plans
- `things-data.js` - starter inventory and structured material ideas
- `moment-ideas.js` - additional low-prep ideas for common family moments
- `things.js` - local inventory, matching, and Idea Builder behaviour
- `play-mode.js` - guided play timer and private activity history
- `activity-photos.js` - Wikimedia Commons image search, licence checking and accessible attribution
- `sw.js` - offline asset cache

## Check And Deploy

This is a static app with no package installation or build step.

```powershell
node --check app.js
node --check things-data.js
node --check moment-ideas.js
node --check things.js
node --check play-mode.js
node --check activity-photos.js
vercel deploy . --prod -y
```

For a local browser check:

```powershell
python -m http.server 8787
```

## Research Sources

The expanded activity set draws primarily from:

- [Australian Government physical activity guidance for birth to 5 years](https://www.health.gov.au/topics/physical-activity-and-exercise/physical-activity-and-exercise-guidelines-for-all-australians/recommendations-for-infants-toddlers-and-preschoolers-birth-to-5-years)
- [Raising Children Network outdoor play](https://raisingchildren.net.au/toddlers/play-learning/outdoor-play/outdoor-play)
- [Raising Children Network preschooler play](https://raisingchildren.net.au/preschoolers/play-learning/getting-play-started/preschoolers-at-play)
- [ABC Kids Early Education Science Time](https://www.abc.net.au/abckids/programs/play-school-science-time)
- [ABC Kids Early Education Make and Create](https://www.abc.net.au/abckids/programs/play-school/play-school-s-make-and-create-extend-play-learn-/105965060)
- [NSW Department of Education play-based learning](https://education.nsw.gov.au/content/dam/main-education/teaching-and-learning/curriculum/early-learning/Play-based-learning.pdf)
- [U.S. National Park Service nature activities](https://www.nps.gov/jomu/learn/kidsyouth/online-activities-and-learning-for-kids.htm)

## More concrete, research-informed instructions (October 2026)

The `development-guidance.js` layer adds concrete worked examples to the most
ambiguous activities and offers separate ways for Sylvie (preschool age) and
Elias (toddler age) to join every idea, including **Our stuff** and Guided Play.
Examples are specific and observable: *draw five big chalk squares, hop/step 1–5,
walk or stomp together to HOME* rather than "invent a mission"; *point to the
tree, move to the bench, return to home base* rather than collecting unknown objects.

The learning notes describe **opportunities to practise**, not guaranteed
outcomes or a developmental assessment. Follow each child's actual interest,
communication, movement and sensory preferences; copying, watching and declining
are valid. Offer a simple choice and demonstrate rather than testing skills.
Keep choking hazards out of toddler activities; supervise water and outdoor play.

Evidence informing the design (not clinical endorsement of individual activities):

- Raising Children Network: [2–3 year development](https://raisingchildren.net.au/toddlers/development/development-tracker-1-3-years/2-3-years), [2–3 year language](https://raisingchildren.net.au/toddlers/development/language-development/language-2-3-years), [4–5 year development](https://raisingchildren.net.au/preschoolers/development/development-tracker/4-5-years).
- Raising Children Network: [Preschool play ideas](https://raisingchildren.net.au/preschoolers/play-learning/getting-play-started/preschoolers-at-play), [Movement play](https://raisingchildren.net.au/preschoolers/play-learning/play-preschooler-development/movement-play-preschoolers).
- Skene et al. (2022), [systematic review of guided play](https://doi.org/10.1111/cdev.13730), Child Development. Effects differed by measured outcome; it is not evidence that any specific activity reliably treats a condition.

Audit: check every activity for clear materials, 2–4 doable steps, concrete
example, choice, age-fit and safety. The default coaching prompts are a
general scaffold, not a claim that every original activity has been
individually rewritten.

# Josh Data Hunt

A private, phone-first personal breach and exposure monitor for Josh and family.

## Current design: free first

Josh Data Hunt works without a paid breach-search subscription.

- **XposedOrNot (XON)** is the default automated breach source. Its community API is keyless and currently limited to 2 requests/second, 25/hour and 100/day per IP.
- **LeakCheck** is checked alongside XposedOrNot as a second free breach source. If one provider is rate-limited, the other can still return a partial result.
- **Have I Been Pwned (HIBP)** remains available as a manual one-tap website check. If a paid HIBP API key is configured later, the existing API integration still works.
- **Intelligence X** remains an optional metadata-only deep-search provider if configured.
- Bulk free scans save their queue in browser localStorage if both free breach sources are rate-limited, so the scan can be resumed later instead of starting again.

## Spreadsheet import

The mobile UI can import the existing Checkup `.xlsx` workbook.

- The workbook is parsed **inside the browser**.
- It is not uploaded to Josh Data Hunt.
- Password, token, secret and TOTP-style columns are ignored.
- Email addresses are deduplicated and shown for review.
- Nothing is searched until the user confirms they own the selected addresses or are authorised to monitor them.
- **Import + scan breaches** adds the selected addresses and starts the free scan queue.

## Privacy model

- Watch-list addresses, free scan results and pending scan queues are stored in browser localStorage on that device.
- App access is protected by a private password and signed HTTP-only session cookie.
- API secrets never go to the browser.
- Josh Data Hunt does not download or redistribute breach dumps.

## Phone use

1. Open the deployed HTTPS site.
2. Sign in.
3. Add addresses manually or choose the Checkup `.xlsx` from your phone/Google Drive file picker.
4. Review the imported addresses and confirm authorisation.
5. Tap **Import + scan breaches** or **Free scan all**.
6. If XON reaches its free hourly/daily limit, leave the saved queue in place and use **Resume scan** later.
7. On Android/Chrome, use **Add to Home screen / Install app** for app-like access.

## Environment variables

Required:

- `APP_PASSWORD` — private dashboard password.
- `SESSION_SECRET` — long random session-signing secret.

Optional:

- `HIBP_API_KEY` — enables paid automated HIBP searches.
- `INTELX_API_KEY` — enables Intelligence X metadata search.
- `INTELX_API_BASE` — Intelligence X API instance, defaulting to `https://2.intelx.io`.

XposedOrNot and the current Hudson Rock OSINT integration require no secret in this app.

Never commit `.env.local`, target addresses, API keys or exported results.

## Local run

```bash
npm install
npm run dev
```

Then open http://localhost:3000.

## Coverage limits

A clean result does not prove an address has never leaked. Each provider has its own dataset, retention rules, exclusions and update timing.

The app therefore reports source-specific evidence rather than claiming to find “everything on the dark web”.

## Roadmap

- Free anonymous exposed-password checker.
- Local encrypted result history.
- “New since last check” comparison.
- Optional scheduled monitoring/notifications without committing personal identifiers.
- Exportable private exposure report.

## Sources

- XposedOrNot: https://xposedornot.com/
- LeakCheck: https://leakcheck.io/
- Have I Been Pwned: https://haveibeenpwned.com/

joshualparris/JoshMemory.readme:
# JoshMemory

JoshMemory is an evidence-aware project continuity system for AI-assisted software development. It helps Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity and other coding workflows resume a project from durable, redacted context while keeping **live Git/API/machine evidence authoritative**.

The default shared-memory design no longer depends on AVANCE-WS7, a home PC or any other workstation remaining powered on. When an existing GitHub credential is available, JoshMemory automatically uses a private GitHub repository as the always-available backing store for handoffs, durable project facts, accountability references, bounded work leases, concise work journals and trust decisions.

## Current architecture

```text
Claude / Codex / Antigravity / JoshMemory MCP
             on any development computer
                         |
                         | existing GitHub authentication
                         v
            private GitHub cloud store
        joshualparris/JoshDashboard4 / main
             joshmemory-cloud/v1/
                         |
             append-only JSON records

Canonical GitHub project + live checkout
             = current code truth
```

The public `joshualparris/JoshMemory` repository contains the software. Shared memory payloads live in the existing **private** `joshualparris/JoshDashboard4` repository and are not exposed through this public source repository.

## What JoshMemory stores

JoshMemory can work with:

- Codex rollout JSONL sessions;
- ChatGPT `conversations.json` exports;
- GitHub evidence JSONL imports;
- seed and app-link imports;
- durable project facts with provenance and supersession;
- accountability references to external verification systems;
- live local Git project state through a cross-platform auditor;
- structured session handoffs/bookmarks;
- bounded current-work leases with heartbeats and expiry;
- concise append-only work-journal events;
- trust decisions kept separate from a fact's factual/status label;
- shared handoffs/facts/accountability/coordination records through private GitHub storage;
- an optional authenticated central HTTP service for the original facts/handoffs API.

Raw transcripts and imported evidence remain source material. JoshMemory stores searchable text, metadata, provenance, relationships and references back to those sources. It does not turn an assertion into truth merely because it was remembered.

## The authority rule

A stored handoff is historical context to verify, not current truth.

When sources disagree, prefer:

1. live repository/API/machine evidence;
2. independently generated verification evidence;
3. explicitly trusted JoshMemory records;
4. ordinary JoshMemory facts, handoffs and journals;
5. older transcripts or inferred context.

For example, if a handoff records one HEAD commit but the checked-out repository now has another, the live repository wins and the discrepancy is reported.

## 2026 portfolio onboarding

For work anywhere in Josh's 2026 coding ecosystem, first read [`docs/CODING_2026_MASTER_HANDOFF.md`](docs/CODING_2026_MASTER_HANDOFF.md) and load/search the shared JoshMemory project **`JoshCoding2026`**. The master handoff reconciles the major 2026 projects, DadLAN/ForgeGrid/local-LLM architecture, engineering-quality model, CRAP4All work, podcast rollout, security/remediation work, CI/deployment lessons, current permission caveats and explicit do-not-redo guidance.

It is deliberately a continuity map rather than a substitute for observation: after reading it, verify the target repository's live Git/CI/deployment/machine state before changing anything.

## Requirements

- Python 3.11+
- GitHub authentication if you want the zero-touch shared cloud store

Install:

```bash
pip install -e .
```

This installs `joshmemory`, `joshmemory-central`, `joshmemory-continuity` and `joshmemory-continuity-mcp`. The original CLI can also be run with:

```bash
python -m joshmemory.cli
```

## Zero-touch cloud shared memory

If the development computer already has GitHub access, JoshMemory looks for a usable credential in this order:

1. `JOSHMEMORY_GITHUB_TOKEN`
2. `GH_TOKEN`
3. `GITHUB_TOKEN`
4. `gh auth token`
5. the configured Git credential helper for `github.com`

It never stores the discovered credential in JoshMemory or commits it to GitHub.

Built-in backing-store defaults for this deployment are:

```text
repository: joshualparris/JoshDashboard4   # private
branch:     main
root:       joshmemory-cloud/v1
```

No AVANCE process, NAS share or always-on local service is required for that mode.

Optional overrides:

```bash
export JOSHMEMORY_GITHUB_STORE_REPO="owner/private-memory-repo"
export JOSHMEMORY_GITHUB_STORE_BRANCH="main"
export JOSHMEMORY_GITHUB_STORE_ROOT="joshmemory-cloud/v1"
```

To deliberately disable automatic GitHub storage and keep the shared operations local:

```bash
export JOSHMEMORY_GITHUB_STORE_AUTO=0
```

### What is shared

The GitHub cloud store centralises the state needed for development pause/resume:

- structured handoffs/bookmarks;
- durable project facts;
- accountability references;
- work-lease events;
- concise work-journal events;
- trust-overlay decisions;
- provenance and supersession for relevant records.

Writes are append-only UUID-named JSON records. Previous records remain available as history; active state is derived rather than rewritten in place.

### What is not silently uploaded

Cloud mode does **not** automatically upload:

- the complete historical SQLite database;
- raw Codex session files;
- complete ChatGPT exports;
- local machine observations;
- other repositories' source code.

This solves shared project continuity without turning the backing repository into an unfiltered transcript dump.

## Cross-machine handoffs

Canonical Git repository identity is the main cross-machine key. A handoff saved from:

```text
~/dev/MyApp
```

can be resumed from:

```text
C:\dev\MyApp
```

when both clones correspond to the same canonical repository. The local checkout path is a ranking preference rather than a global identity barrier.

A typical startup flow is:

1. identify the local project and canonical repository;
2. load the latest relevant handoff;
3. audit live branch/HEAD/dirty state;
4. surface discrepancies;
5. check whether another agent already owns the work item;
6. continue from the first still-valid next action;
7. save a new handoff at a meaningful checkpoint, blocker or session end.

## Coordination and memory governance

JoshMemory 0.3 adds the strongest compatible ideas from open-source coding-agent memory systems without copying their implementation code. See [`docs/CONTINUITY_COORDINATION.md`](docs/CONTINUITY_COORDINATION.md) and [`docs/OPEN_SOURCE_MEMORY_BORROWING_PLAN.md`](docs/OPEN_SOURCE_MEMORY_BORROWING_PLAN.md) for design rationale and provenance.

### One-command resume brief

A fresh agent can ask for the latest handoff, live-state discrepancies, active lease, recent journal entries and next action in one result:

```bash
joshmemory-continuity resume DCSPD \
  --canonical-repo github.com/joshualparris/DCSPD \
  --agent codex \
  --work-key ci
```

If another agent currently owns the same work key, the resume result includes an explicit collision warning rather than encouraging duplicate work.

### Work leases

Claims are bounded by a TTL and can be heartbeated or released:

```bash
joshmemory-continuity claim DCSPD --owner codex --work-key ci --ttl 900
joshmemory-continuity heartbeat DCSPD --owner codex --work-key ci
joshmemory-continuity release DCSPD --owner codex --work-key ci
```

Local SQLite claims use transactional serialization. The GitHub cloud store is append-only and therefore uses truthful optimistic claim/election semantics rather than pretending GitHub provides database row locks.

### Append-only work journal

Store short redacted milestones instead of transcript dumps:

```bash
joshmemory-continuity journal-add DCSPD TEST "Playwright smoke passed" \
  --details-json '{"run":"35277769767"}'

joshmemory-continuity journal DCSPD
```

### Trust is separate from status

A fact being `CURRENT` or `OBSERVED` does not mean a human approved it. The separate trust overlay is:

- `UNTRUSTED` — agent/import context, useful but not endorsed;
- `VERIFIED` — checked against cited evidence;
- `APPROVED` — explicitly accepted by an operator/reviewer;
- `SYSTEM` — deterministic system-produced state.

Agents cannot self-promote memory above `UNTRUSTED` through the continuity API. Trust promotion is an operator action and `VERIFIED` requires a source reference. This is governance, not an authentication substitute: live evidence still wins.

## Default local paths

- Codex sessions: `~/.codex/sessions/**/*.jsonl`
- local SQLite index: `~/.local/share/joshmemory/memory.sqlite`
- projects: `JOSHMEMORY_PROJECTS_DIR` when set; otherwise `C:\dev` on Windows when available, or `~/dev`

The local SQLite index remains useful for historical/offline search. It is not the cross-machine merge object.

## Optional HTTP central service

JoshMemory still supports the authenticated HTTP service added for traditional central-server deployments.

If `JOSHMEMORY_REMOTE_URL` is configured, it takes precedence over automatic GitHub storage:

```bash
export JOSHMEMORY_REMOTE_URL="https://your-joshmemory-service"
export JOSHMEMORY_TOKEN="your-private-bearer-token"
```

Once an explicit HTTP remote is selected, failures are surfaced rather than silently falling back to a local database and creating split-brain shared memory.

The original HTTP service currently covers the facts/handoffs/accountability API. The 0.3 coordination record families intentionally fail explicitly if that legacy HTTP backend is selected; use local storage or the default GitHub-backed store for leases, journals and trust until the HTTP protocol is extended.

The included Dockerfile and Fedora deployment helpers remain available. They are optional; AVANCE-WS7 is not required for cloud continuity.

See [`CLOUD_DEPLOYMENT.md`](CLOUD_DEPLOYMENT.md) for details.

## MCP servers

Start the original stdio MCP server with:

```bash
python -m joshmemory.server
```

Current original-server tools include:

- `search_sessions`
- `get_session`
- `project_history`
- `recent_work`
- `github_evidence`
- `project_status`
- `historical_search`
- `earliest_activity`
- `historical_timeline`
- `project_fact_search`
- `accountability_search`
- `save_handoff`
- `get_project_context`
- `list_handoffs`

For coordination-aware coding agents, start the companion MCP server:

```bash
joshmemory-continuity-mcp
```

It exposes:

- `resume_brief`
- `claim_work`
- `heartbeat_work`
- `release_work`
- `active_lease`
- `list_leases`
- `append_work_event`
- `recent_work_events`
- `memory_trust`
- `trusted_fact_search`

There is deliberately no agent-facing trust-promotion tool.

Existing Claude SessionStart/SessionEnd/Stop integration continues to use the handoff storage layer and live-Git reconciliation.

## CLI examples

Index and search local historical material:

```bash
joshmemory index
joshmemory search FedoraCrashDoctor
joshmemory project-history FedoraCrashDoctor
joshmemory recent-work
```

Import evidence:

```bash
joshmemory import-seed /path/to/seed.json
joshmemory import-app-links /path/to/app-links.json
joshmemory import-github-evidence evidence.jsonl
joshmemory import-chatgpt /path/to/chatgpt-export --dry-run
joshmemory import-chatgpt /path/to/chatgpt-export
```

Historical retrieval:

```bash
joshmemory historical-search "what were we coding in March 2023?"
joshmemory earliest-activity coding
```

Add/search durable facts:

```bash
joshmemory add-fact \
  --project AgentWitness \
  --subject deployment \
  --fact "Windows verifier installed" \
  --status VERIFIED \
  --source-type receipt \
  --source-ref AGY-20260827-example

joshmemory search-facts verifier --project AgentWitness
```

Fact statuses are `VERIFIED`, `OBSERVED`, `HISTORICAL`, `INFERRED`, `STALE`, `DISPROVEN`, `U

# Paul Roe Archive

Private research archive compiled from Josh's connected sources on **19 September 2026**.

## Coverage

- **Gmail:** 309 messages matching `Paul Roe`, 146 matching `paul.roe@cornerstone.edu.au`, plus 7 additional `Paul Rowe` spelling matches. The combined archive contains **316 unique Gmail references/messages**. Full readable bodies are stored in `gmail/full-messages-*.md`, with separate context indexes and source links.
- **Google Drive:** **763 unique matching non-trashed items** after de-duplicating Drive IDs across searches for `Paul Roe`, `paul.roe@cornerstone.edu.au`, and `Paul Rowe`. No matching items were found in Drive Trash. Canonical indexes are `drive/all-matches-001.md` onward, with source links; high-relevance text contexts are also included where Drive exposed readable text.
- **Google Calendar:** all **28 accessible calendars** were searched by name across 2000–2035. **4 matching events** were found, all in the primary Cornerstone calendar. Email-address and `Paul Rowe` cross-checks on Cornerstone-related calendars produced no additional events.
- **GitHub:** all five connected GitHub owners/installations were checked. No exact `Paul Roe`, Paul Roe email-address, or exact `Paul Rowe` references were found outside this archive; broad code-search hits were verified as unrelated false positives.
- **ChatGPT Library:** supplementary ranked searches were saved under `library/`. These are useful cross-references to Library copies/reports but Library search is ranked/paginated rather than an authoritative exhaustive filesystem scan.

## Search identifiers

Primary identifiers used:

- `Paul Roe`
- `paul.roe@cornerstone.edu.au`
- `Paul Rowe` (recurring historical misspelling)

Gmail was also checked with `in:anywhere` so Spam/Trash were not silently omitted.

## Privacy

This repository is **private** and contains personal correspondence and other non-public material. Keep it private unless individual material is reviewed for sharing.

## Structure

- `gmail/` — full messages, match-context indexes, spelling cross-check
- `drive/` — complete Drive-ID indexes, Trash check, selected extracted contexts
- `calendar/` — searches across all accessible calendars and identifier cross-checks
- `github/` — connected-account scans and false-positive evidence
- `library/` — supplementary ChatGPT Library search results
- `analytics/` — private, durable daily aggregate website analytics

## Memorial website

A public memorial website lives in `site/`.

It is intentionally separated from the private research archive so deploying the memorial does **not** expose private Gmail, Drive or family correspondence.

The memorial includes:

- Paul's public story and legacy
- Cornerstone Community and Bourke connections
- The Outback Historian project
- books, podcasts, interviews and video
- a remembrance timeline
- links to original public sources
- mobile-friendly sharing and accessibility support

Deployment workflow: `.github/workflows/pages.yml` uploads **only** the `site/` directory to GitHub Pages.

## Private browsable archive

The private research browser starts at [`private-archive/README.md`](private-archive/README.md).

It provides clickable navigation through Gmail, Drive, Calendar, public-web research, ChatGPT Library and GitHub scan material. It is explicitly excluded from the public GitHub Pages build.

## Private memorial analytics archive

Vercel Web Analytics for the public memorial is archived under [`analytics/vercel-web-analytics/`](analytics/vercel-web-analytics/).

A scheduled GitHub Action queries the official Vercel Web Analytics API and stores only daily page-view and unique-visitor totals using the **Australia/Sydney** calendar. It deliberately excludes visitor IDs, IP addresses, referrers and user-agent data.

The archive begins from **22 September 2026**, when Vercel Web Analytics was enabled. The workflow automatically backfills missing days once the private repository has a `VERCEL_TOKEN` Actions secret.

# ResearchLibrary

A private, Dewey-inspired catalogue linking Josh's deep-research repositories and documents without duplicating their evidence or changing the source repositories.

## Start here

- **[Master research catalogue — browse subjects, GitHub repos and Google Drive folders](docs/github-research-library.md)**
- [Machine-readable repository and folder index (JSON)](catalogue/repositories.json)
- **[Browse 311 classified research topics by Dewey subject](docs/individual-research-documents.md)** — direct Google Drive document links
- **[Document-level Dewey audit — 889 research documents, 311 title groups](docs/document-level-dewey-audit.md)**
- [Searchable machine-readable document index (JSON)](catalogue/drive-documents.json)
- [Likely distinct research topics and candidate duplicates (JSON)](catalogue/drive-topic-groups.json)
- [Classification decisions and evidence for the 84 formerly unclassified groups](catalogue/classification-review-2026-10-15.json)
- [ResearchAtlas — discovery and interactive research frontend](https://github.com/Parris-Tech-Services/ResearchAtlas)
- [ResearchGems — recall and spaced-repetition tools](https://github.com/Parris-Tech-Services/ResearchGems)

## How the library works

Each research repository stays authoritative for its source evidence, citations and revision history. The catalogue gives it a **primary three-digit subject shelf** plus cross-references. The numbers are a practical Dewey-inspired navigation system, **not** a claim that all assigned numbers are fully verified official DDC classifications.

The expanded catalogue covers **32 research and research-adjacent GitHub repositories**, **28 Google Drive research folders**, and a metadata inventory of **889 research text documents** grouped into **311 provisional title groups** (plus five software support files; zero remaining unclassified items), updated **15 October 2026**. Source content remains in the original locations. It is not yet an exhaustive inventory of every repository or research document. New repos should be reviewed for relevance and privacy before adding them.

### Privacy

This repository is **private**. Some linked repositories contain confidential correspondence or personal data. **Do not make this repository public or mirror its catalogue into public sites** without reviewing all titles, summaries, document paths and links. Link targets retain their own GitHub access controls. This catalogue **does not replicate** underlying private research or personal datasets.

## Mirror

The initial catalogue originated in [ResearchAtlas](https://github.com/Parris-Tech-Services/ResearchAtlas). This repository maintains an additional copy for GitHub-first browsing. The two copies are **not automatically synchronised**, so changes need to be reflected in both until a sync workflow is implemented.

## Research-depth notes

The document-level audit is a metadata and filename analysis, **not** verified deduplication of full text or a complete recursive Google Drive scan. The subject chart based on unique repositories/folders should not be used as a substitute for the document-level distribution. The full index also includes **104 ancillary files and five software support files** for provenance (media, code and ZIP bundles), excluded from research-topic counts.

## AI-assisted deep research methodology (October 2026)

# Tristan Harris — life, influence and work in 2026

> Independent, source-linked research dossier. **Research cut-off: 13 October 2026 (Australia time).** This repository documents **public professional activity**, not private personal details. Statements about influence are distinguished from demonstrable policy outcomes.

## At a glance

**Tristan Harris** is a technology ethicist, entrepreneur, former Google design ethicist, and co-founder of the [Center for Humane Technology (CHT)](https://www.humanetech.com/). His signature argument: incentives that reward harvesting attention or accelerating AI capability can work against human wellbeing. He helped popularise the **Time Well Spent** movement, was a central voice in the 2020 Netflix documentary *The Social Dilemma*, and now works to change incentives governing advanced AI. [CHT history](https://www.humanetech.com/impact-and-story) · [Personal site](https://www.tristanharris.com/).

### What he is specifically doing in 2026
1. **Public-facing AI risk education** — appearing in *The AI Doc: Or How I Became an Apocaloptimist*, released in US cinemas 27 March and on Netflix in September, and joining interviews, talks and documentaries.
2. **Briefing and convening leaders** — at Davos, Milken, the ITU AI for Good summit, the September Pro-Human Assembly and Telluride, with cross-partisan outreach.
3. **Advocating safeguards and coordination** — discussing frontier AI race incentives, developer accountability, safety testing, AI companion risks to children, and potential US-China cooperation.
4. **Leading a new CHT strategy** — an **October 1 board announcement** says CHT is winding down in-house policy, litigation and research in favour of founder-led communications, targeted briefings and private coordination. WIRED reported nine staff departures on October 8; ex-employees dispute the wisdom of the change.

**Important distinction:** Being interviewed by policymakers or appearing near legislative activity does not by itself show that Harris wrote, passed, or caused a law. Statements about audience reach from CHT and film publicity are estimates or self-reports, not independent measurements.

## Newly investigated: 90 questions and their evidence-based answers (13 October 2026)

The [90-question gap register](research/08-open-questions-inventory.md) was **committed before the investigation**, then researched question by question. All 90 entries have a public-evidence answer, partial response, contested explanation, or explicit **not established** status.

**Start here: [all 90 answers and findings index](research/02-evidence-based-answers.md).**

| New audit | Details |
|---|---|
| [Questions Q01–Q44](research/09-evidence-based-answers-part-1.md) | Early life, education, beliefs, social-media science, AI theory |
| [Questions Q45–Q64](research/10-evidence-based-answers-part-2.md) | AI predictions, lawmakers, policy and causal impact |

| [Finances, impact and corrections](research/12-impact-finances-and-corrections.md) | **FY2025 public IRS 990**, CHT revenue/spending, compensation, donor channels, published corrections |

**Important corrections to the original overview:** official public [Form 990 figures](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/organizations/823492182) replace vague budget estimates; a **February Harris–Yoshua Bengio recording confirms Davos activity**; the **2017 precursor / 2018 CHT formation** distinction is retained; and the [CHT Davos episode](https://www.humanetech.com/podcast/the-race-to-build-god-ais-existential-gamble-yoshua-bengio-and-tristan-harris-at) includes explicit corrections to Harris's statements. These findings clarify the older documents, which are retained as the initial research pass.

## Deep investigation: Chinese Amap AI-agent fleet (13 October 2026)

**[Read the full investigation and conclusions](research/15-chinese-amap-agent-fleet-deep-investigation-2026.md)**. A dedicated deep dive into Swarmchasers' September–October 2026 evidence: Tencent Cloud/hysandbox callbacks; more than 2,000 narrow fleet scanner reports; venue entrance-share readouts; independent versus coordinated agents; attribution uncertainty; and substantial **9 October corrections** to the investigators' preliminary account.

- [Technical evidence, competing interpretations and corrected statistics](research/16-amap-fleet-evidence-and-attribution-audit.md)

**Research integrity note:** **1,810** is a count of *scanner reports* on 4 October, **not 1,810 AI agents**. **14** is a peak *inferred concurrent-run count*, **not a confirmed number of independent agents**. The actual operator, model and possible coordination remain unverified. The 13 October follow-on survey counts all Amap-related observations, **not just this fleet**. [Original investigators](https://swarmcha.se/posts/chinese-agent-fleet) · [13 October survey](https://swarmchase.alecto.dev/).

## New: autonomous agent swarms on the internet (13 October 2026)

**[Autonomous AI-agent swarms: verified 2026 research, experiments and real incidents](research/14-autonomous-ai-agent-swarms-online-2026.md)** — evidence-led investigation prompted by a report of former Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon's October testimony. Includes OpenAI's Hugging Face containment failure and improvised agent-to-agent message board, Anthropic's 45-agent studies and October IoT self-replication experiments, Moltbook/OpenClaw/Pilot Protocol, online agent fleets, practical security safeguards and open questions. **Distinguishes controlled experiments and unverified projections from live incidents and actual coordination.**

## New: Practical personal application (private, 13 October 2026)

**[Start here — what to change, what to protect, and what not to worry about](personal/00-read-me-first.md).** A source-linked personal response to the whole dossier, including a life-domain matrix and priorities.

# Whispering Wilds

A robust, data-driven text adventure game. Originally a simple prototype, the engine has been completely rewritten to support clean data pipelines, determinism, and robust state management.

---

## Quick start

### 1. Install Dependencies
```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

## Engineering standard

Engineering principles: v5.1  
Assurance tier: 1  
Canonical repository: https://github.com/joshualparris/Whispering-Wilds

### 2. Choose Your Interface
**Whispering Wilds now features two interfaces.** Both use the exact same underlying game engine and share the same save data. You can save in the CLI and load your game in the TUI without losing progress.

**Option A: The Textual TUI (Recommended)**
A rich, split-pane dashboard with real-time stats and an interactive map.
```bash
PYTHONPATH=src python3 src/tui.py
```
*TUI Controls: Type commands into the input box or click the quick-action buttons with your mouse.*

**Option B: The Classic CLI**
The original text adventure experience.
```bash
PYTHONPATH=src python3 src/main.py
```

In game, try:

```text
help
look
take rust_key
move e
use rust_key
move e
map
```

---

## Architecture & Features

The game features a data-driven engine.

* **Content Pipeline:** Rooms, items, quests, and bestiary are defined in JSON inside `src/content/`.
* **State Management:** All player data is tracked explicitly in `GameState` (`src/engine/state.py`), ensuring clean persistence and zero data-loss on restart.
* **Deterministic E2E Testing:** The engine uses a fully deterministic `CLIHarness` with 100% test coverage for quests, economy, and combat mechanics.

### Core Systems
- **Combat:** Genuine random encounters based on the bestiary. `attack` to deal damage, `flee` to escape. Status effects (bleed, poison, chill) impact player health over time.
- **Quests:** Interact with NPCs (`talk caretaker`, `say 1`) to accept and turn in quests.
- **Gathering & Crafting:** `forage`, `mine`, `fish`, `harvest`, and `craft` items to survive the wilderness.
- **Save/Load:** Native JSON saving system. Use `save` to store your session to a file, and `load` to resume.

---

## Core commands

```text
help | look | map | stats | inv
move n/s/e/w  (or: go n/s/e/w)
take <item>   | drop <item>   | use <item>
equip <item>  | unequip <item>
talk <npc>    | say <n>

attack | rest | bandage | flee

forage | mine | fish | harvest | craft <thing>
buy <item> | sell <item>

note <text> | journal | erase <n> | hardmode on/off
save | load

bestiary | lore <creature>
quests

ascend (Watchtower completion)
quit
```

---

## Development & Testing

**Requirements:**
- Python 3.9+
- `textual` (for the TUI)
- `pexpect` (for the E2E test suite)

**Running Tests:**

We provide a robust E2E test suite covering gameplay flows.

```bash
PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```

joshualparris/dewey-converter-for-librar.readme:
# Dewey Helper for LibraryThing

**Use it now:** https://dewey-helper.vercel.app

A free, open-source browser tool for librarians and small libraries who want to review Dewey Decimal Classification (DDC) values in a LibraryThing catalogue.

This project is the 2026 successor to the original `dewey-converter-for-librarything` idea. The old workflow depended on OCLC Classify, which was discontinued in 2024, and on automating LibraryThing catalogue edits. The replacement deliberately avoids scraping or automated LibraryThing logins.

## What it does

1. Export your own LibraryThing catalogue as **Excel (.xlsx)**, Tab-Delimited Text, CSV or JSON.
2. Open Dewey Helper in your browser and select the export.
3. The app extracts ISBNs locally.
4. When you press **Find Dewey numbers**, it sends batched ISBN lookups to Open Library.
5. It checks the exact ISBN edition first using Open Library's multi-book Books API. If that exact edition has no DDC, it can use Open Library's work-level Search API as a clearly labelled fallback.
6. It shows the current LibraryThing DDC beside the best free-data candidate, with a confidence/review status.
7. You can edit suggestions and export the reviewed results as TSV, CSV or JSON.

Your original export is never modified.

## Privacy and safety

- No LibraryThing username or password is required.
- Your catalogue file is parsed in your browser, not uploaded to this project.
- Excel files are parsed client-side with SheetJS Community Edition 0.20.3, loaded from SheetJS's pinned official CDN.
- ISBNs are sent to Open Library only after you start a lookup.
- Results are cached locally in your browser to reduce repeat API traffic.
- This project does **not** scrape LibraryThing and does **not** automate catalogue editing.

LibraryThing currently provides user catalogue exports but no supported API for editing members' books. Their terms also prohibit unapproved scraping/automated site access, so Dewey Helper intentionally leaves final catalogue changes to the human librarian.

## Data source

The free version uses [Open Library](https://openlibrary.org/) because it provides open, public book metadata and can return Dewey values when they exist in its records.

Lookup order:

1. **Exact edition first:** a batched Books API request checks the specific ISBN and uses its edition-level `dewey_decimal_class` when present.
2. **Work-level fallback:** if the exact edition has no Dewey value, the Search API may return DDC values aggregated across editions of the ISBN-matched work. These are always marked **Needs review** and are never presented as exact-edition classifications.

Open Library asks apps not to make hundreds of single-book calls. Dewey Helper therefore:

- batches ISBNs;
- waits at least about one second between Open Library requests;
- caches prior responses locally;
- does not automatically retry unresolved books via high-volume fuzzy searches.

A result is a **cataloguing aid, not an authority record**. DDC can vary by edition, library policy and cataloguing judgement. Review suggestions before applying them.

## LibraryThing export

LibraryThing currently offers Excel, Tab-Delimited Text, JSON and MARC exports at https://www.librarything.com/export. **Excel (.xlsx) now works directly** in Dewey Helper, as do Tab-Delimited Text, CSV and JSON exports.

Typical LibraryThing export fields include:

- `Book_Id`
- `Title`
- `Primary_Author`
- `ISBN`
- `ISBNs`
- `Dewey_Decimal`
- `Dewey_Wording`
- `OCLC`
- `Work_id`

The importer is tolerant of common alternative field names.

## Run locally

There is no build process.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/joshualparris/dewey-converter-for-librarything.git
cd dewey-converter-for-librarything
python -m http.server 8000
```

Then open `http://localhost:8000`.

You can also open `index.html` directly, although browsers sometimes apply stricter network rules to local `file://` pages.

## Project principles

- free to use;
- no paid API required;
- no credentials;
- no scraping;
- human review before catalogue changes;
- accessible to non-programmers;
- minimal dependencies;
- pinned SheetJS Community Edition only for Excel import;
- respectful API usage.

## Limitations

Open Library does not have a Dewey number for every ISBN. Some exact editions have no DDC even when another edition of the same work does. Work-level fallbacks and multiple candidate DDC values are intentionally marked for review rather than silently treated as authoritative.

This tool currently does not write data back into LibraryThing. A supported LibraryThing member-book editing API would be the right way to add that in future.

## Licence

MIT. See [LICENSE](LICENSE). Third-party software notices are in [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md).

## Disclaimer

Not affiliated with LibraryThing, OCLC, the Dewey Decimal Classification system, the Online Computer Library Center, Open Library or the Internet Archive. Dewey Decimal Classification and DDC are trademarks of OCLC. Metadata quality varies; librarians remain responsible for classification decisions.

- [Julie Gibson Clark](docs/people/julie-gibson-clark.md) — unusually transferable working-parent longevity routine and a very low reported DunedinPACE

### Measurement / quantified-self case studies

- [Bob Troia](docs/people/bob-troia.md) — years of practical N-of-1 tracking across body composition, sleep and glucose
- [Michael Snyder](docs/people/michael-snyder.md) — peer-reviewed personal multi-omics and disease-detection research
- [Larry Smarr](docs/people/larry-smarr.md) — long-term biomarker tracking that helped surface persistent inflammation before Crohn's diagnosis

Snyder and Smarr are deliberately included as **measurement lessons, not "healthiest person" claims**. Being deeply measured and being disease-free are different things.

## Research documents

- [Metric-by-metric comparison](docs/comparison.md)
- [Low-cost working-family playbook](docs/practical-playbook.md)
- [Time/cost/family transferability matrix](docs/transferability.md)
- [Research backlog / known data gaps](docs/research-backlog.md)
- [Evidence quality, conflicts and interpretation](docs/evidence-and-bias.md)
- [Public data access audit](docs/data-access-audit.md)
- [Normalised metrics dataset](data/metrics.csv)

## Purpose

This project asks three separate questions:

1. What does the best publicly available evidence actually show about each person's health or physiology?
2. What does their measurement strategy teach us, even when they are not disease-free?
3. Which parts are realistically transferable to an ordinary middle-class adult who works five days a week, has children, bills, stress, limited time, and no private medical team?

The project does **not** claim the public case studies are literally the healthiest humans alive. Public datasets are incomplete, collected at different ages and dates, and often use different methods.

## Evidence rules

Every specific health claim should be classified by source quality:

- **A — independent peer-reviewed / institutional measurement**
- **B — independently reported clinical or laboratory result**
- **C — first-party published measurement or protocol**
- **D — self-report / interview**
- **Unknown — insufficient provenance**

We prefer current measurements over historical peak values, but preserve both when useful.

## Practical translation

For each person, separate:

- **High-value / low-cost:** behaviours an ordinary family can realistically copy.
- **Useful but optional:** measurements or equipment that may help but are not necessary.
- **Expensive / low-transferability:** concierge medicine, frequent imaging, experimental therapies, elaborate testing and other interventions that should not be presented as prerequisites for good health.

## Website files

- `index.html` — homepage and daily dashboard
- `styles.css` — responsive design
- `site-data.js` — evidence-aware case-study + working-parent lesson dataset, curated listening library and weekly routine
- `app.js` — Sydney-time daily rotation and filters
- `vercel.json` — Vercel static-site configuration
- `.github/workflows/pages.yml` — keeps the `gh-pages` publishing branch current
- `.github/workflows/validate.yml` — checks JavaScript syntax and page wiring on every push
- `standalone.html` — portable self-contained copy of the current site

No framework, database, tracking script or paid API is required.

## Safety and interpretation

This repository is educational research, not personalised medical advice. Association is not causation, exceptional individuals are not universal templates, and a biomarker that is unusual is not automatically desirable.

# The Undercity

**A playable, original, gothic narrative RPG for your browser.**

In a city beneath a sealed stone sky, memories can be traded, lamps burn on peculiar fuel and official records erase people who are still alive. You start in the Bell-Cage, choose your past and faction, escape by one of four approaches, and decide who should learn the truth about the sky.

## Play now

**Current updated playtest: https://undercity-playtest.parris-neathaustralia.workers.dev/**

The original https://the-undercity.vercel.app deployment is currently behind GitHub because Vercel reached its daily Free-plan deployment limit. The Cloudflare alternative has passed an external HTTP smoke check on game HTML, rules JS, and new late-ambition content. The two sites use different browser-local save storage; export a JSON save before switching.

The current tested game is published from this repository on Cloudflare Workers as a pinned GitHub-source snapshot. Vercel remains a secondary, older deployment. No sign-in or payment is required. Saves are **local to the browser and device** you use, not synchronised across phones and computers. Export a JSON save from **Settings** before clearing browser data or switching devices.

## Narrative production pipeline

**[Open the QBN Studio CMS](tools/cms/index.html)**\n\n**[Groq AI writing assistant — setup and safety](tools/cms/GROQ_AI.md)**: 14 creative and editorial workflows, private server-side Groq gateway, proposal review, and AI-ready handoff exports for both games. Groq generation requires two private Cloudflare Worker secret bindings; no credentials are stored in this repository. to draft branching stories and export review packets.

**[Narrative Studio](docs/narrative-studio/README.md)** defines our pitch → midflight skeleton → prose → four QA reviews → human approval process. Its 40-topic spoilers ledger tracks reveal depth and deliberately conflicting witness accounts. Use `npm run studio:validate` before releasing new storylets; editorial drafts are not loaded by the running game.

## What is playable

- Story-driven onboarding: four backgrounds, five factions, four ability-based escape routes leading to distinct districts.
- A connected city map with clear roads and unlock requirements. Collect **2 leads** for the Forgotten Stairs and **4 leads** for the Listening Edge.
- A four-stage city investigation about the Council's sealed sky, with different world outcomes.
- **Four original personal ambitions**, now with **32 consecutive storylets apiece**. The Moth King's later chapters are authored in versioned JSON; River, Mirror and Ember each have 24 new later chapters in a separate narrative module, with ending choices and persistent consequences.
- **Four seven-stage Making Your Name reputations**, one for each ability, with distinct progress and end rewards.
- The four abilities **Observation, Guile, Persuasion and Resolve**, using the level-70 CP pyramid, parameterised Broad and fixed Narrow checks, rare-success rolls, and 1–2 CP awards.
- **34 professions** (10 Tier 1, eight Tier 2, eight Tier 3, eight Tier 4). Senior careers require in-world promotion storylets, relevant reputation and previous office; each has its own pay, shift stories and professional equipment.
- **20 destinies** (9 ordinary, 11 greater), with eligibility gates and permanent selection.
- **9 character quirks**, **3 three-stage exceptional stories**, and **6 rotating seasonal events**.
- **352 storylets and 854 authored choice branches**, plus 18 opportunity cards, including multiple stat-gated and origin-dependent decisions. See the [full content tracker](docs/CONTENT_TRACKER.md).
- **20 equipment slots**, at least one purchasable item for each, additive skill bonuses, and a buy/sell Bazaar with 20 goods. Selling equipped gear removes its active bonus.
- Four **Living Stories** using a persistent, author-defined event queue with quality triggers, hour delays, related story IDs, and visible countdowns in Messages.
- Ten-minute action regeneration with a starting cap of 10 and an unlockable cap of 20; four-minute opportunity-card regeneration with six-card hand limit. **Settings → Playtest mode** removes waiting/paid card-draw costs for testing.
- Four pyramidal Menaces (**Suspicion, Notoriety, Wounds, Delirium**) with zero-action arrival scenes, three recovery methods per hub, and a permanent arrest Record capped at seven. Fourteen quality categories are registered in the narrative schema. Card draw rules include urgent-card bypass, unlock-condition weighting and full-hand pause.

The UI includes semantic navigation landmarks, a keyboard skip link, adjustable persistent text size, and a colorblind/high-contrast option. Actual automated Chromium smoke and axe WCAG A/AA checks passed at 390px and 1280px. Manual TalkBack, VoiceOver, NVDA and real-device testing remain outstanding.

## How to playtest

1. Begin at the Bell-Cage, choose an origin and faction, and take one of the four escape routes.
2. Use **City map** for explicit connections. Lantern Court links to the main starting districts.
3. At Lantern Court, speak to the clockmaker to begin the city-wide investigation, and choose a **personal ambition** using *A question no clerk can answer*.
4. Open **Paths & callings** to see the next stage and district for your ambition, all four reputations, career options, quirks, exceptional stories and destiny requirements.
5. Visit **Possessions** to equip owned gear, and **Messages** for delayed Living Stories.
6. Test success and failure, a full opportunity hand and a menace-triggered recovery detour. Use **Settings → Playtest mode** if you want to inspect content without waiting.
7. Export your save JSON before restarting or switching browsers.

## Narrative authoring and checks

- The **JSON-authored** late Moth chapters live in `content/storylets/ambitions/moth.json`. The River, Mirror and Ember late-main arcs are authored in `content/storylets/ambitions/late-main.v1.json` and compiled to `content/late-ambitions.js` by `scripts/build-late-main.mjs`. Another 66 optional investigations use versioned JSON in `content/storylets/ambitions/second-acts.v1.json`, compiled by `scripts/build-second-acts.mjs`. The coalition conclusion in each arc requires earlier independent evidence and protected witnesses.
- `node scripts/build-content.mjs`, `node scripts/build-second-acts.mjs` and `node scripts/build-late-main.mjs` compile the canonical JSON content. Use `--check` to catch out-of-date browser bundles.
- `node scripts/validate-content.mjs` validates story references, locations, challenge qualities, item effects and chain gates.
- `node scripts/content-tracker.mjs` updates `docs/CONTENT_TRACKER.md` with every story, choice, card, location and profession; use `--check` to detect drift.
- GitHub Actions runs the checks and game tests on each push. Vercel's project build command is configured to run all three validation steps as well.

## Repository and checks

The game is dependency-free plain HTML/CSS/JavaScript. The canonical QBN engine lives in `src/game/rules.js` (ES module); `rules.global.js` is its byte-verified classic-script build loaded by the browser. Existing v1 local saves are migrated into the richer qualities schema without resetting progress. Narrative data is in `content/`. Tests in `tests/` run through GitHub Actions on each push. Run locally with `node --test tests/*.test.mjs` (Node 22+) and serve the repository with `python -m http.server 8000` if you want to test it on a local server.

## Specification scope and remaining work

The supplied 64-page research PDF is much larger than a single release. **All four ambitions now meet the 30–40 chapter count target**, but further authored branching, character-specific dialogue and NPC consequences are still needed for the full depth requested. Early-stage stories and some other content still use JavaScript predicates, and there is no web-based CMS, cross-player social system, cloud account/save service, or fully developed crafting economy. The story and mechanics remain independently authored.

See [Specification coverage and roadmap](docs/SPEC_PROGRESS.md) for explicit implemented/partial/not-yet-built status and the next planned systems. The setting, characters and prose are independently authored rather than copied from other games.

## Narrative CMS · QBN Studio

The same no-code editorial workflow is available in the [Undercity Studio](https://the-undercity.vercel.app/tools/cms/), adapted to Observation, Guile, Persuasion and Resolve, the city's own locations and local save-compatible runtime. Create branches, challenge gates and outcomes, export drafts, and use stage-specific AI briefs without an exposed API key.

Read the [studio workflow](tools/cms/WORKFLOW.md), [world bible](tools/cms/bible.md), [proposed secrets ledger](tools/cms/secrets.md) and [style guide](tools/cms/style.md). Human-approved individual JSON enters `content/storylets/cms/<story-id>.json`; run `npm run cms:build && npm run cms:check && npm test`, then refresh the content tracker. Drafts stay in the author's browser until exported. Current collaboration is file/PR-based rather than simultaneous editing.
